A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRASP research. All 15 pages of v3 and 16 pages of v4, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V3 reports original GRASP accuracy, perplexity, compression-time, throughput, and ablation results in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds retain-ratio experiments and comparisons with SparseGPT and Wanda.

M1.justification: Cosine-similarity layer selection, gradient-based singular-group scoring, reverse layer processing, and optional post-training remain unchanged. Changing 'top-k' to 'top-r%' and explicitly identifying calibration-data use clarify the procedure already described in v3's Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Training, calibration, and evaluation coverage is retained, including reasoning benchmarks, NLU/QA, GSM8K, LongBench, and WikiText-2/PTB. The new retain-ratio and sparse-pruning comparisons reuse existing reasoning tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix A.9 and Table 15 add evaluated SparseGPT and Wanda comparators using 2:4 sparsity. Neither participated in v3's reported comparisons, although the Wanda work was cited. Existing structured-pruning comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V4 adds a 0–20% retain-ratio sweep over eight LLaMA2-7B layers and compares 50%-sparse SparseGPT/Wanda with GRASP at 20% structured compression. Table 2's caption changes from 20% to 25%, matching the setting already stated in v3's prose; this correction does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Section 3.4, Table 6, and Figure 6 add a sensitivity study testing how singular-group retention affects compression and accuracy. Existing calibration-data and pruning-strategy ablations are retained; the latter's table merely moves from the appendix into the main text.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All matched existing table entries and plotted results remain unchanged. New Table 6 reports average accuracy of 41.1, 45.5, and 45.8 at 0%, 10%, and 20% retention. New Table 15 reports averages of 46.28 for SparseGPT, 45.16 for Wanda, 45.27 for GRASP, and 50.01 for compensated GRASP under the differing compression regimes.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the low-rank assumption, and Appendix A.1's singular-value gradient derivation are unchanged. Added compression-budget explanations and SVD positioning do not introduce a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: gradient-guided replacement of redundant layers, training-free compression, and inexpensive post-training recovery. The abstract's claim of retaining 90% performance at 20% compression is unchanged.

C2.justification: V4 interprets saturation beyond 10% retention as support for that default and for redundancy in selected layers. Appendix A.9 adds a qualification about sparse formats complicating compression comparisons. Section 7's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 explicitly identifies calibration-data use, Appendix A.3 explains how layer selection and retention jointly determine overall compression, and Section 3.3 defines pruning versus compensation timing. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, and the underlying code-repository link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds the SparseGPT reference and discussion of sparse-pruning comparisons. Section 5 adds an argument about square-matrix SVD parameter savings and information loss. The added 2023 Wanda reference describes the same work already cited through its 2024 publication in v3.

P1.justification: Descriptive comparison headings replace 'Experiment 1–3', Section 2.2 receives limited wording edits, and explanatory appendix sections are added. The pruning-strategy appendix material is consolidated into Section 3.4; the overall narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: V4 adds Figure 6 and Tables 6 and 15. V3's Table 10 moves into the main text as Table 7, other tables are repositioned or renumbered, and Table 2's caption is corrected. Existing figures and table structures are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: The new retain-ratio study supplies empirical support for the previously used 10% choice, while compression explanations and the Table 2 caption correction reduce ambiguity. SparseGPT/Wanda comparisons add useful context, but their differing compression regimes limit conclusions about comparative efficiency. These are modest gains in evidence and clarity, with the original method and results retained.
